title: Action Verification through Conjecture and Refutation for Language Model Agents
title_zh: 通过猜想与反驳实现语言模型智能体的动作验证

paragraphs.en: 提出BlackSwan反驳式动作验证程序,通过预期、怀疑与检验显著提升语言模型智能体成功率。 Language model agents increasingly act on users' behalf by manipulating external environments through tools, often from high-level instructions that leave critical task- and environment-specific context unstated. To prevent resulting misaligned actions, recent work verifies proposed actions before execution, largely by establishing whether the conditions supporting them hold. We argue that this confirmation-oriented view leaves a fundamental blind spot: a wrong action often passes every check that asks whether it is right. This motivates a different question for verification: rather than asking what evidence supports an action, can the agent find evidence that refutes it? We pursue this direction with BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented, expect-suspect-test procedure that predicts the intended effect of each state-mutating action, formulates specific and empirically testable hypotheses for how it could be wrong, and tests them using existing observations or additional non-mutating actions, executing the action only if none survives testing. On challenging AppWorld tasks, BlackSwan improves success rate over the strongest baseline by 14.9 and 25.2%p with and without the backbone model's thinking mode, respectively. Even without thinking or in-context demonstrations, it outperforms stronger baselines equipped with them. The gains also transfer beyond AppWorld, with BlackSwan improving WebShop performance by 12.7%p. More broadly, our results suggest that language model agents have an underused capacity to recognize and self-correct misaligned actions, which can be systematically elicited through active conjecture and refutation before execution.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出BlackSwan，一种反驳式的动作验证程序，通过预期、怀疑与检验显著提升语言模型智能体的成功率。语言模型智能体越来越多地通过操作外部环境来代表用户执行任务，而这些操作往往源自高层指令，其中关键的任务相关与环境相关的背景信息常常未被明说。 为了防止由此产生的不一致动作，近期的工作在执行前对拟议动作进行验证，主要是通过确认支持该动作的条件是否成立。 我们认为，这种以确认为导向的视角存在一个根本性的盲区：一个错误的动作往往能通过所有询问“它是否正确”的检查。 这启发我们提出一个不同的验证问题：与其询问有什么证据支持某个动作，智能体能否找到反驳它的证据？ 我们沿着这一方向提出了BlackSwan，这是一种以反驳为导向的“预期—怀疑—检验”程序：它预测每个会改变状态的动作的预期效果，为该动作可能出错之处制定具体且可实证检验的假设，并利用现有观察或额外的非改变状态的动作来检验这些假设，只有当所有假设均未能通过检验存活时才执行该动作。 在具有挑战性的AppWorld任务上，在使用与不使用骨干模型思考模式的情况下，BlackSwan分别将成功率比最强基线提升了14.9个百分点和25.2个百分点。 即使不使用思考模式或上下文示例，它也优于配备了这些手段的更强基线。 这些收益还可以迁移到AppWorld之外，BlackSwan将WebShop的性能提升了12.7个百分点。 更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，语言模型智能体具有一种尚未被充分利用的能力，即识别并自我纠正不一致动作的能力，而这种能力可以通过在执行前主动进行猜想与反驳被系统地激发出来。
